title: Lessons with Manetta, method book, jazz and ragtime repertoire
summary: She used a beginner method book with Manetta only to learn to read, picked up jazz herself, and recalls playing old rags such as Panama and Red Rose Rag.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Can you remember anything about your lessons with Professor Renetta? Did he, what books or anything else he might have used or how he taught you? So I see I've gone to some of his lessons on the clarinet and also a friend of mine that took a few piano lessons once, a boy from Chicago. And do I know something about his teaching? I just wondered in those days back then.
I only used the James Belloc.
James, I'm not even familiar with that.
James Belloc.
It was a regular method book?
A regular method, a beginner.
Yes.
And then after I went to St. Maher's Academy, well, I had to take music with them.
Yes.
You see, I took music with them.

I know today Professor Renetta doesn't teach much in the line of jazz or improvising and, you know, just playing popular tunes. He sticks mostly to the more classical music and their methods. Yes, he did. Did he do that when you were studying with him too or did he ever help you with some of the late tunes?
Oh, no. Well, you see, I didn't need any help on the plane.
You were able to pick those right up anyway.
Yeah. I just took lessons to learn to read. To read, no. But I didn't need any help at all on the plane because I started out in the jazz time.
Yes.
And when I played with my brothers, well, it was swing time.
A lot of times in the old days, about that time, they were calling it rag time too, weren't they?
Well, rag time too, yeah.
Do you remember any of the old rags, like the Joplin rags and all? Professor Renetta still played some of those. I was the old playing ball.
I don't remember. We played some of them.
Well, like Panama always. Yes, Panama. Of course, they used the other night.
Red Rose Ray. Oh, yes. Sensation is plenty. Oh, yes. All those old days. Yes. Oh, we play all that. Still good numbers, actually. Oh, wonderful. They're wonderful numbers.
